papers.title: Aging, Structural, and Neighborhood-Environmental Correlates of Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Risk Factor Burden Across U.S. Census Tracts
papers.abstract: Background. The American Heart Association defined Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome in 2023. Census-tract studies often examined one condition without spatial modeling. It is unclear where combined Stage 1-2 burden concentrates and how it relates to aging, environment, and socioeconomic conditions. Methods. We built a CKM burden index for 70,336 tracts from five CDC PLACES crude prevalences (obesity, diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, chronic kidney disease) and compared it with NHANES 2017-2020. In 69,530 contiguous-U.S. tracts, we fit Bayesian spatial (BYM2) models with demographic, socioeconomic, and environmental predictors and aging x environment interactions, plus descriptive machine learning. The primary model excluded behavioral measures sharing the outcome's BRFSS source; a second added them. Credible intervals (CrIs) are conditional on PLACES estimates. Results. Agreement with NHANES was modest. Burden clustered spatially (Moran's I = 0.657) and highest in the South. Behavioral measures had the largest machine-learning importance (52.6%), partly from shared sourcing. Each percentage-point increase in adults 65 years was associated with 0.112 units higher burden (95% CrI 0.111-0.113) outside low-income, low-access (LILA) tracts. LILA tracts had 0.10-0.14 units higher burden from the 25th aging percentile but not consistently in the youngest decile. Aging and socioeconomic associations held across sensitivity analyses. The primary model's residual Southern excess approached zero after adding behavioral measures, which may reflect shared measurement, real differences in these behaviors, or both. Conclusions. CKM burden is spatially clustered and highest in the South. LILA tracts had modestly higher burden above the youngest tracts. These cross-sectional estimates support area-level surveillance and needs assessment.

papers.title: Gut microbiome associations with incident cardiovascular disease in Nordic populations
papers.abstract: Background: The gut microbiome is an emerging risk factor for cardiovascular disease. However, there is a lack of large-scale metagenomic studies with replication that identify gut microbial features associated with incident cardiovascular disease (CVD). Methods: We tested for gut microbiome associations with CVD using metagenomes from stool samples in a discovery-replication framework across four large prospective Nordic cohorts with 635 incident CVD in 11,604 participants in the discovery cohort and 2,309 incident CVD in 20,965 participants combined across three replication cohorts. Results: Higher Shannon diversity index and species richness were consistently associated with a lower risk of incident CVD. In addition, the relative abundance of nine species and eleven bacterial functional modules showed reproducible associations with incident CVD in the discovery cohort and in a meta-analysis of the three replication cohorts. We identified a female-specific gut microbiota-related pathway involving the prevalent oral-gut species Rothia mucilaginosa_A, enriched among denture users, thus serving as a proxy for longstanding poor oral health. Mendelian randomization analysis supported a causal effect of denture use on increased relative abundance of Rothia mucilaginosa_A. This pathway was linked to increased CVD risk through altered gut microbial manganese transport, elevated circulating imidazole propionate levels, and increased levels of systemic inflammation biomarkers. The second pathway involved both ?-diversity metrics and the remaining eight species, all of which were strongly associated with multiple markers of metabolic syndrome and with bacterial pathways related to purine metabolism, microbial stress responses, altered redox balance, ascorbic acid degradation, and branched chain amino acid biosynthesis. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate that gut microbiota diversity, specific taxa, and functional pathways provide new insights into the underlying biology of CVD. Furthermore, these findings suggest that the link between poor oral health and cardiovascular disease may, at least partly, operate through altered gut microbiota.

papers.title: The gut microbiome and incident atherosclerotic cardiovascular events: Prospective analyses in three Swedish cohorts
papers.abstract: Background: Variation in the gut microbiome composition has been associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) in case-control designs. We aimed to investigate associations with incident ASCVD events applying a prospective design to reduce the impact of reverse causality. Methods: We assessed associations between gut microbiome features measured by shotgun metagenomic sequencing and incident total ASCVD, ischemic heart disease (IHD) and ischemic stroke, including fatal and non-fatal events as defined by registry follow-up in 17,216 participants from three Swedish population-based cohorts (SCAPIS, SIMPLER, and MOS). Results from Cox proportional hazards regression models adjusted for demographic, and lifestyle factors, medication, and prevalent diabetes were combined across cohorts using a fixed-effect meta-analysis accounting for multiple testing. Associations were tested for replication in HUNT and FINRISK. Results: During a median of 6-8 y follow-up, 769 incident ASCVD events occurred. Species diversity was inversely associated with ASCVD and IHD, with a hazard ratio for IHD of 0.86 per SD increase in species richness (95% CI: 0.79-0.95). Sixty-eight common species (i.e., present in ?30% individuals) were associated with incident IHD after adjusting for sex and birth country, but only eight remained in fully adjusted models, including Ruminococcus_B gnavus. Among others, inverse associations were observed for SFEL01 sp004557245 and Fimadaptatus sp900553645 from Christensenellales, an order in which butyrate production has been reported. Streptococcus mutans and Limosilactobacillus fermentum, oral-associated species previously associated with coronary atherosclerosis, were associated with a higher risk of incident IHD, which remained after adjustment for dental health. Replication analysis in the HUNT study supported the finding for S. mutans. No associations were observed with ischemic stroke. Conclusions: Gut species diversity and specific species abundance were associated with incident IHD, providing evidence supporting a protective role of two Christensenellales species and an adverse role of oral species and R. gnavus in the development of IHD.

papers.title: Projected prevalence and number of persons with diagnosed type 2 diabetes by socioeconomic position in Germany between 2022 and 2060
papers.abstract: Background: Current projections of the prevalence and number of persons with type 2 diabetes by socioeconomic position (SEP) are lacking for Germany. This study aims to project age-specific type 2 diabetes prevalence in Germany by sex and SEP between 2022 and 2060. Methods: We used a partial differential equation (PDE) based on the illness-death model to project age-specific type 2 diabetes prevalence by sex and SEP between 2022 and 2060. The PDE describes the relationship between prevalence, incidence, all-cause mortality and the mortality rate ratio (MRR) of individuals with vs. without type2 diabetes considering age, calendar year and SEP. SEP was measured by quintiles of the German Index of Socioeconomic Deprivation (GISD). Baseline prevalence, incidence, and MRR in 2022 were derived from statutory health insurance data (~85% of the German population). Projected prevalence was multiplied by population projections from the German Federal Statistical Office to estimate the number of persons with diabetes. Results: Type 2 diabetes prevalence increases with age, peaking between 80 and 90 years. Between 2022 and 2060, age-specific prevalence is projected to increase for both sexes across all SEP groups. SEP-related disparities persisted with largest differences between the highest (5th GISD quintile) and lowest (1st GISD quintile) SEP group. The number of persons with type 2 diabetes is projected to rise from 8.4 million in 2022 to between 11.2 and 19.2 million in 2060. Conclusions: Between 2022 and 2060, age-specific type 2 diabetes prevalence is projected to increase with increasing socioeconomic inequalities.

papers.title: Investigating Differential Changes in Cardiovascular Mortality by Documented diabetes in the United States Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Comparative Time-Series Analysis
papers.abstract: Background: Whether diabetes modified pandemic-related changes in cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality remains uncertain. We examined differential changes in US CVD mortality among deaths with versus without diabetes documented on the death certificate. Methods: We analyzed CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death data from 2005 to 2024, identifying deaths with CVD as the underlying cause among adults aged 25 years. Cohorts were CVD deaths with diabetes documented as a contributing cause (CVD+DM) and CVD deaths without documented diabetes. Because pre-2020 trajectories differed, the primary comparison of age-adjusted rates used a comparative interrupted time-series model allowing cohort-specific pre-2020 trends. Difference-in-differences estimates (2015-2019 vs 2020-2024) were descriptive. Results: CVD+DM mortality declined from 43.1 per 100,000 in 2005 to 34.3 in 2019 and was 38.4 in 2024; mortality without documented diabetes declined from 398.7 to 296.6 and was 289.8. In the primary analysis, CVD+DM mortality showed a 13.1% greater relative level increase at 2020 (95% CI, 10.4%-15.9%), with no significant differential change in slope thereafter. Descriptively, the ratio of rate ratios was 1.16, and the absolute difference-in-differences was 5.0 per 100,000. Conclusions: After accounting for cohort-specific pre-2020 trends, CVD mortality with documented diabetes showed a greater relative increase at the 2020 transition. These findings describe differential mortality patterns rather than a causal effect of diabetes or the pandemic. Keywords: Cardiovascular mortality; Diabetes; COVID-19; Difference-in-differences; Preventive Cardiology Nonstandard Abbreviations and Acronyms AAMR: age-adjusted mortality rate APC: annual percentage change CITS: comparative interrupted time-series CVD+DM: cardiovascular disease deaths with diabetes documented as contributing cause DID: differences-in-differences DM: diabetes mellitus

papers.title: Sex specificity in DNA Methylation Profiles of Neonates Following Early Preterm Birth
papers.abstract: Preterm birth (PTB) affects 11% of pregnancies worldwide, yet the biological mechanisms underlying its etiology remain unclear. We conducted a sex-stratified epigenome-wide association study of newborn saliva DNA methylation in 273 mother-child pairs from the Peruvian Placental Abruption Genetic Epidemiology (PAGE) study. Robust linear regression models adjusted for maternal, cellular, and technical factors identified 318 and 542 ePTB-associated CpG sites and 784 and 1,401 differentially methylated regions in boys and girls, respectively, with limited overlap between sexes. Functional analyses revealed enrichment of signals in Open Sea regions and pathways related to neurodevelopment, neural function, fetal growth, cellular organization, transcription factors, and microRNAs. Several associations replicated findings from prior studies of PTB, gestational age, and post-menstrual age. These results identify sex-specific epigenetic signatures of ePTB in an Admixed-American population and highlight developmental and regulatory pathways associated with ePTB.

papers.title: A deterministic framework for linkage of infectious disease surveillance and national mortality records: development and validation using tuberculosis surveillance data
papers.abstract: Background: Linkage of infectious-disease surveillance data to mortality records is important for estimating long-term outcomes, but incomplete personal identifiers present methodological challenges. We developed and validated a deterministic linkage framework for linking the National Tuberculosis Surveillance System (NTBS) with Office for National Statistics (ONS) mortality records. Methods: TB notifications in England from 2001 to 2024 were linked to ONS mortality records using 12 sequential matching rules based on combinations of NHS number, date of birth, name, postcode, sex and phonetic matching. Linkage outputs underwent person level deduplication and clerical review. Precision and recall were estimated, and potential linkage bias assessed by variation in identifier completeness and linkage success. Confirmed false-positive links identified during validation were removed from the analytical dataset. Results: Among 151,965 TB notifications, 28,060 initial links were identified. Following deduplication, validation and refinement, 26,937 linked notifications were retained. Estimated precision increased from 97.7% to 99.2% (95% CI 96-100.0) following removal of false-positive links; estimated recall was 98.1% (95% CI 95.4-98.6%). More than 90% of links used NHS-number-based match keys. PDS enrichment increased NHS-number availability and enabled additional NHS-number-based links, although a small proportion linked to different ONS records following enrichment. NHS number availability and linkage success differed across demographic and social groups, demonstrating differential linkage. Conclusions: A hierarchical deterministic approach combined with targeted validation achieved high linkage accuracy while identifying and addressing differential linkage. This provides a transparent framework for future NTBS-ONS linkage and may be adaptable to other surveillance systems where comparable identifiers are available.

papers.title: Real-world effectiveness of nirsevimab over three RSV seasons in an integrated health care system: a target trial emulation study
papers.abstract: Most nirsevimab effectiveness estimates come from test-negative designs, which restrict populations to those seeking healthcare and testing. We estimated nirsevimab effectiveness among infants six months post-receipt using a target trial emulation with an estimand aligned to phase 3 trials. We emulated a target trial among infants born from February 2, 2023 through May 30, 2026, using electronic medical records at Kaiser Permanente Georgia. Using a g-computation estimator with Cox models fit separately in nirsevimab recipients and non-recipients, we estimated the cumulative incidence of RSV hospitalization and medically-attended RSV at 30-day intervals through 180 days post-receipt. Among 4,826 infants, nirsevimab reduced the risk of RSV hospitalization by 95% (95% CI: 84% to 98%) and medically-attended RSV by 67% (95% CI: 45% to 80%) at 180 days post-receipt. The number needed to immunize to prevent one case was 147 (95% CI: 94 to 333) for RSV hospitalization and 39 (95% CI: 28 to 68) for medically-attended RSV. Nirsevimab was effective through 180 days post-receipt. This cohort-based emulation avoids conditioning on testing and the restricted generalizability of the test-negative and matching-based designs that dominate the literature. These findings support continued nirsevimab use to protect infants against RSV.

papers.title: Intersectional inequalities in demand satisfied by modern contraceptive methods among women in sub-Saharan Africa, 1994 to 2024: a multilevel analysis of individual heterogeneity and discriminatory accuracy
papers.abstract: Background: Demand for family planning satisfied by modern methods is Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) indicator 3.7.1, and countries have committed to universal access to family planning by 2030. Inequalities are usually reported one social dimension at a time. This hides how social characteristics combine and leaves open whether programmes should target social groups or strengthen services for all women. We measured intersectional inequalities in demand satisfied by modern methods among women in sub-Saharan Africa over three decades, assessed how well social position discriminates between women, and identified groups left behind. Methods and findings: We did a preregistered cross-sectional analysis of 139 Demographic and Health Surveys from 38 countries with fieldwork from 1994 to 2024. We included 675,584 women aged 15-49 years with demand for family planning and grouped them into 144 intersectional strata by age, union status, education, household wealth and residence. We fitted multilevel logistic models with random effects for strata and surveys (multilevel analysis of individual heterogeneity and discriminatory accuracy, MAIHDA) and estimated the variance partition coefficient (VPC), the area under the curve (AUC) and the proportional change in variance (PCV). Weighted demand satisfied rose from 27.5% in 1994-99 to 54.1% in 2018-24. Predicted demand satisfied ranged from 13.2% (95% CI: 11.0 - 15.9) among married adolescents with no schooling in the poorest rural households to 68.0% (95% CI: 63.6 - 72.0) among unmarried urban women aged 25-34 years with secondary schooling in the richest households. The strata explained only 6.9% (95% CI: 5.6 - 8.7) of individual variation, with small discriminatory accuracy (AUC = 0.65; 95% CI: 0.63 - 0.66), and a Bayesian model gave a similar VPC (7.0%; 95% credible interval: 5.7 - 8.9). Additive effects explained 95.1% of the between-stratum variance. The VPC fell from 10.1% (95% CI: 8.0 - 12.8) in 1994-99 to 4.5% (95% CI: 3.6 - 5.8) in 2018-24. Five strata of married rural women with no schooling were in the lowest decile in every period. In the latest surveys, married rural women aged 15-24 years with no schooling had lower demand satisfied than other women in 29 of 30 countries (median gap 17.5 percentage points). The 15 most disadvantaged strata held a median 16.4% of unsatisfied demand, so targeting these groups alone would reach about one in six women whose demand is not met. The main limitations are the cross-sectional design, self-reported contraceptive use and the exclusion of 15 early surveys. Conclusions: Intersectional gaps in demand satisfied by modern methods have narrowed in sub-Saharan Africa, and most of the remaining gap between groups is additive. Social position alone discriminates poorly between women, so programmes targeted only by social group would miss most women with unmet need. This supports strengthening universal services. Within universal services, married adolescents and young women with no schooling in poor rural households have been left behind for three decades in almost every country and need priority, country-specific programmes if the 2030 targets are to be met.

papers.title: Direction of apoB/LDL-C Discordance and Systemic Inflammation in U.S. Adults
papers.abstract: Background: Apolipoprotein B (apoB) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) are established biomarkers of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) that tend to be closely correlated. However, some individuals have discordant apoB and LDL-C. We evaluated whether apoB/LDL-C discordance is associated with elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), a key marker of systemic inflammation, in a nationally representative sample. Methods and Results: We analyzed 2226 adults aged 20 years or older from the 2015 to 2016 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey with complete apoB, LDL-C, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP). LDL-C and apoB were converted to survey-weighted scores, and discordance was the residual of apoB regressed on LDL-C. Participants were classified as apoBhigh, LDL-C-high, or concordant (reference). The association of discordance group with elevated hs-CRP (>3 mg/L) was estimated with survey-weighted logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), and diabetes. Discordance was present in 26.4% of adults (13.7% apoBhigher, 12.6% LDL-C-higher). Elevated hs-CRP prevalence differed by discordance group: 47.6% (95% CI, 37.6?57.7) in the apoB-high group versus 20.5% (12.9?28.1) in the LDL-C-high group and 33.6% (29.7?37.4) in the concordant group. Relative to concordant participants, adjusted odds of elevated hs-CRP were higher for apoB-high discordance (odds ratio [OR], 1.58; 95% CI, 1.03?2.45) and lower for LDL-C-high discordance (OR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.30?0.78). Similar results were obtained among participants not on statin therapy, with apoB-high discordance demonstrating stronger adjusted odds of elevated hs-CRP (OR, 2.02; 95% CI, 1.01?4.04). Conclusion: Discordantly high apoB relative to LDL-C is associated with systemic inflammation in a nationally representative sample of U.S. adults.

papers.title: Smoking trajectories and brain health in middle-aged adults: a 15-year longitudinal study
papers.abstract: Background. Smoking is a prevalent and preventable risk factor for poor brain health. These habits often establish in early adulthood and have lasting consequences, yet most research focuses on later-life smoking, overlooking important prevention windows. We examined smoking trajectories from early adulthood in relation to midlife brain health. Methods. In 1,900 adults (65.6% female, mean age 32.5 years) from the Dutch population-based Generation R Study (ORACLE subset), smoking was assessed five times over 15 years, from before pregnancy to midlife. K-means clustering identified smoking trajectories, alongside measures of current smoking, pack-years, and abstinence years. At mean age 47.7 years, MRI assessed gray and white matter volumes, white-matter hyperintensity volume, cerebrovascular markers, and vertex-wise cortical thickness and surface area. Findings. Five trajectories were identified: non-smoking (63%), quitting before pregnancy (12%), quitting during/after pregnancy (11%), relapsing (9%), and persistent smoking (4%). All compared with non-smoking, quitting before pregnancy was associated with 6.57 cm3 larger gray matter (95%CI[0.27,12.87],p=.041), 7.71 cm3 larger white matter (95%CI[0.77,14.65],p=.030), and larger cortical surface area in bilateral middle/inferior temporal regions. Quitting during/after pregnancy was associated with more lacunes (OR=2.39; 95%CI[1.23,4.68],p=.011), but similar brain volumes. Relapsing was associated with 0.15 standard deviations more white matter hyperintensity volume (95%CI[0.00,0.30],p=.045) and thinner regions in the right cortex. Persistent smoking had double white matter hyperintensities (0.31 standard deviations; 95%CI[0.10,0.50], p=.003) and widespread bilateral thinner cortices. Similarly, single-timepoint measures like current smoking (vs never smoking) were linked to 9.72 cm3 smaller gray matter volume (95%CI[-16.53,-2.19],p=.005), 0.17 standard deviations more hyperintensity volume (95%CI[0.03,0.32],p=.015), and widespread thinner cortices. Each additional pack-year was associated with 0.45 cm3 smaller gray matter volume (95%CI[-0.85,-0.06],p=.025); each additional abstinence year was associated with 0.01 standard deviations less hyperintensity volume (95%CI[-0.02,0.00],p=.022). Interpretation. Smoking trajectories from early adulthood and midlife are associated with midlife brain health, supporting early and sustained smoking cessation.

papers.title: Age at Menopause and Dementia Risk: Blood-Based Biomarker Evidence from a US National Study
papers.abstract: Importance: Earlier age at menopause associates with increased later life dementia risk, but the biological links that underlie this relationship remain poorly understood in population-based samples. Objective: To evaluate the relationship between history of menopausal timing and AD/ADRD-related blood-based biomarkers in postmenopausal women. Design: Observational study using the U.S. Health and Retirement Study. AD/ADRD-related biomarkers were measured from venous blood draws conducted in 2016 and released in 2025. We estimated linear and nonlinear associations between spontaneous menopause timing and biomarkers, accounting for sociodemographic and health covariates. We evaluated effect modification by APOE {varepsilon}4 carrier status. Secondary analyses evaluated associations with hysterectomy history. Setting: Population-based. Participants: Community-dwelling post-menopausal women aged 65 years or older. Exposure: Primary: Self-reported spontaneous age of menopause among women with no history of hysterectomy. Secondary: Self-reported history of hysterectomy (oophorectomy history was not assessed). Main Outcomes and Measures: Neurofilament light chain (NfL) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) measured in plasma, and phosphorylated tau (p-tau181) and growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF-15), measured in serum, by Simoa or ELLA. Results: Among 1449 women [≥]65 years, 38.4% self-reported a hysterectomy. Among 893 postmenopausal women without a history of hysterectomy (mean [SD] age at biomarker collection, 75.2 [7.2] years; mean age at menopause, 50.2 [5.2] years), menopausal timing was nonlinearly associated with NfL. Between menopausal ages 45-50, menopause timing was associated with higher NfL (0.010 SD units/year, [95% CI: -0.007, 0.027]), while from menopausal ages 50-55, the association reversed (b= -0.031, [95% CI: -0.051, -0.011]). Associations with GFAP or pTau-181 were not significant, but were directionally similar to those observed for NfL. Later menopausal timing linearly associated with lower GDF-15 (b = -0.015, [95% CI: -0.027, -0.004]). Self-reported hysterectomy was associated with higher GDF-15 (b= 0.118, [95% CI: 0.015, 0.220]), but not other biomarkers. Associations did not significantly differ by APOE {epsilon}4 status. Conclusions and Relevance: In a nationally representative study, earlier age at menopause in midlife was associated with later life AD/ADRDs biomarkers reflecting neuroaxonal degeneration and inflammation, underscoring the importance of understanding reproductive aging in dementia risk.

papers.title: Weighting the weeks that matter: entropic tilting for epidemic forecast evaluation
papers.abstract: The performance of infectious disease forecasting models is commonly calculated under the implicit assumption that forecast accuracy is equally important across time. This approach may obscure or under-weight differences in model performance during the epidemic periods that matter most for public-health decisions. Here, we introduce the weighted prequential score (WPS), a forecast evaluation framework that can emphasize epidemic periods of interest. The WPS is a weighted average of scores over time, where weights are constructed through entropic tilting which up-weights priority periods while keeping the WPS as close as possible to the arithmetic average. We demonstrate the WPS on forecasts of incident hospitalizations submitted to the CDC FluSight challenge, focusing on two priority periods: weeks of rapid growth in incidence and weeks near the seasonal peak. Across season-location-horizon pairs, doubling the weight assigned to priority periods changes the top-ranked model in 10%-26% of eligible settings, while the top-ranked model remains unchanged regardless of the amount of weight assigned in 37%-68% of settings. We demonstrate that for suitable weights, the models favored by the WPS yield an average gain in accuracy during priority periods that is at least as large as the average accuracy lost during the remaining weeks. Because weights can be defined using observed outcomes, the WPS is not a proper scoring rule. Hence, we recommend using the WPS as a retrospective evaluation diagnostic. The WPS can guide public-health practitioners in selecting models that perform well during periods most relevant to their decisions, while encouraging forecasting teams to improve accuracy during these critical weeks.

papers.title: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Risk of Colorectal Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.abstract: Epidemiologic studies suggest that type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with an increased risk of colorectal cancer (CRC). However, prior meta-analyses have relied heavily on studies published more than a decade ago and have often combined distinct epidemiologic effect measures. We conducted an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies published from January 2012 through January 2026 evaluating the association between T2DM and incident CRC. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and Scopus were searched, and eligible studies reporting associations between T2DM and CRC were included. Effect estimates were synthesized separately using random-effects models to calculate pooled estimates with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sex-specific and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were also conducted. Fourteen studies were included, comprising nine cohort and five case-control studies; six reported odds ratios (ORs), seven reported hazard ratios (HRs), and one reported a standardized incidence ratio (SIR). T2DM was associated with higher odds of incident CRC (OR, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.13-1.46) and a higher hazard of incident CRC (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.23-1.31). The study reporting an SIR also showed higher CRC incidence among individuals with T2DM (SIR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.39-1.45). Sex-specific analyses generally showed positive associations in both females and males, and sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the pooled findings. Overall, T2DM was associated with an increased risk of incident CRC, with a consistent direction of association across distinct epidemiologic effect measures. These findings provide updated evidence supporting consideration of T2DM as a marker of increased CRC risk and may inform CRC prevention strategies among individuals with T2DM.

papers.title: Prevalence of Self-Reported Auditory Dysfunction Among Call Center Employees and Its Association with Shift Work Across Various Call Centers in Cairo, Egypt, March 2026
papers.abstract: Abstract Background The rapid, unregulated expansion of the call center industry in developing countries has increased occupational health risks for young adults, particularly with regard to auditory health. Prolonged exposure to acoustic trauma, long working hours, and the high intensity nature of call center work can negatively affect young adults at the start of their working lives and may contribute to permanent noise induced hearing loss (NIHL). This damage is often irreversible but preventable if identified at an early stage. This study aims to evaluate the burden of auditory impairment among call center employees in Egypt and to propose evidence based mitigation strategies. Methods A pilot cross sectional study was conducted among employees of various medical call centers over approximately three months (January to March 2026). Participants were recruited through voluntary (self selected) sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire on work history, and statistical analysis was performed to examine associations with work duration and intensity. Three semi structured, open ended interviews were conducted in March 2026 to explore the symptoms in greater depth. Results Forty six call center employees completed the questionnaire. The most frequently reported symptoms were mishearing words (82.6%), difficulty understanding speech in background noise (80.4%), needing others to repeat themselves (78.3%), and sensitivity to loud sounds (78.3%); 60.9% reported tinnitus. Higher auditory symptom severity was associated with a history of acoustic shock (Mann Whitney U = 344.0, p = .004) and with greater cognitive symptom burden (Spearman's {rho} = .416, p = .004), but not significantly with shift type (p = .177), years of work (p = .885), or daily and weekly working hours. Qualitative interviews described auditory strain that builds through the shift, disrupted sleep, informal coping, and the absence of employer guidance or symptom reporting pathways. Conclusion and Recommendations Self reported auditory symptoms were common in this preliminary sample of call center employees and were associated with acoustic shock exposure and cognitive symptom burden, but not significantly with shift pattern or length of service. Because the study was cross sectional, relied on self reports, and used a small volunteer sample (pilot study), the findings cannot establish causation or true prevalence. Recommended measures include acoustic shock limiters with incident reporting, audiometric screening that prioritizes at risk employees, safe volume education with regular breaks, and educational programs on auditory hazards and early warning signs to prevent actual auditory damage. Larger multi site studies with audiometric confirmation are also needed. Keywords: noise induced hearing loss; call center employees; occupational health; auditory dysfunction; tinnitus; acoustic shock; shift work; Egypt

papers.title: Pneumococcal nasopharyngeal carriage in children 2-60 months of age in Novi Sad (Serbia), October 2022-September 2026
papers.abstract: Background: Streptococcus pneumoniae nasopharyngeal carriage in young children is an important source of transmission and may precede pneumococcal disease. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines can alter circulating serotypes. Continued surveillance is needed to monitor serotype replacement, vaccine serotype coverage, and antimicrobial resistance. Methods: A prospective surveillance study was conducted in outpatient pediatric practices from October 2022 to September 2026 among children aged 2-60 months in Novi Sad, Serbia. Healthy children attending preventive visits and children with acute respiratory tract infections were enrolled. Nasopharyngeal specimens were collected and cultured for S. pneumoniae. Participant-level analyses used the first eligible specimen per child, while isolate-level analyses included all recovered isolates. Serotyping and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed. Theoretical vaccine serotype coverage was estimated for licensed and selected investigational pneumococcal conjugate vaccines, with 23-valent polysaccharide vaccine evaluated separately. Results: Among 3,373 included children, 911 were pneumococcal carriers, giving an overall carriage prevalence of 27.0%. Carriage was higher among children with acute respiratory tract infection than among healthy children and was also associated with daycare attendance, chronic medical conditions, age, season, and surveillance year. In total, 1,312 pneumococcal isolates were recovered, of which 87.9% were typeable. The most frequent serotypes included 11A, 10A, 15A, 15B, 23A, 23B, 19A, and 6B. Theoretical serotype coverage was 8.2% for PCV10, 17.5% for PCV13, 20.0% for PCV15, and 47.3% for PCV20. More than half of typeable isolates were non-PCV20 serotypes. Resistance was most frequent to erythromycin, clindamycin, and tetracycline, while multidrug resistance was observed in 18.1% of isolates. Penicillin G non-susceptibility was uncommon. Conclusion: Pneumococcal carriage in children aged 2-60 months in Novi Sad was associated with age, clinical presentation, season, and surveillance year and involved diverse serotypes. Continued carriage surveillance, linked with invasive-disease and antibiotic-use data, would help determine whether the observed serotype and resistance patterns persist.

papers.title: Socioeconomic position, socioenvironmental conditions, and subjective cognitive decline among midlife and older LGBTQIA+ adults in California
papers.abstract: Objectives: To examine which measure of socioeconomic position and socioenvironmental conditions has the strongest relationship with subjective cognitive decline (SCD) among midlife and older lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex, asexual, and other sexual and gender minority (LGBTQIA+) adults. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 3869 LGBTQIA+ adults aged 50 years or older participating in a community-engaged survey in California. Using logistic regression, we examined overall associations between each indicator of socioeconomic position and socioenvironmental conditions and SCD. We used a dominance analysis to assess the relative importance of each indicator based on the proportion of variance in SCD it explained. Results: Overall, 14.7% of the sample reported SCD. Midlife and older LGBTQIA+ adults in a lower socioeconomic position (i.e., lower education, unemployment, lower household income, fewer assets, financial insecurity, food insecurity, and unstable housing) had higher odds of SCD than those in a higher position, with significant odds ratios (OR) ranging from 1.44 to 1.93. In contrast, perceiving one's community as safe for LGBTQIA+ people was associated with lower odds of SCD (OR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.48, 0.76). Dominance analysis indicated that household assets was the most important factor, explaining 2.8% of the variance in SCD (95% CI 2.2%, 3.6%), followed by household income (1.9%; 95% CI 1.2%, 2.7%) and perceived community safety (1.6%; 95% CI 1.1%, 2.3%). Discussion: Supporting the cognitive health of LGBTQIA+ people may require attention to both financial security across the life course and the broader social environments.

papers.title: Epidemiology of zero-dose among children aged 12-35 months in Ethiopia: Burden, correlates and spatial patterns; Evidence from a 2025 national survey
papers.abstract: Background: Children who have not received the first dose of a diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis-containing vaccine are classified as zero-dose. Understanding how many children remain without this dose beyond infancy, the correlates, and their geographic distribution can inform routine and catch-up vaccination services in Ethiopia. This study aimed to estimate the burden of zero-dose, identify its correlates, and map its spatial distribution among children aged 12-35 months in Ethiopia. Methods: We analyzed data from 2,097 children aged 12-35 months in the Pathways for Ethiopia survey, a recent national population-based cross-sectional household survey conducted from August to November 2025. The burden estimates and regression analyses accounted for sampling weights, stratification, and clustering. Adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) were obtained through marginal standardization of survey-weighted logistic regression models. Spatial autocorrelation, hotspot, and spatial-scan analyses assessed geographic clustering. Ordinary kriging predicted prevalence at unsampled locations. Results: The weighted prevalence of zero-dose status was 20.6% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 15.9-26.3), with regional point estimates ranging from 0.8% in Addis Ababa to 35.9% in Somali. Its burden was 20.4% among children aged 12-23 months and 20.8% among those aged 24-35 months. Higher burden was associated with no antenatal care compared with four or more visits (aPR: 2.39; 95% CI: 1.61-3.53), unimproved compared with improved drinking-water sources (aPR: 1.52; 95% CI: 1.18-1.97), and caregivers rating vaccination as less than very important compared with very important (aPR: 2.68; 95% CI: 2.03-3.54). Zero-dose prevalence showed significant spatial clustering (Morans I = 0.229; p = 0.0001). Hotspots occurred among sampled communities in Somali, Oromia, Central Ethiopia, Afar, and South Ethiopia. Predicted prevalence was highest across parts of eastern and south-central Ethiopia. Conclusion: Approximately one in five children aged 12-35 months had not received the first pentavalent dose. High zero-dose prevalence clustered among sampled communities in eastern and south-central Ethiopia. Moreover, antenatal care and drinking water source were independent factors. Immunization programs should prioritize these communities for identifying and vaccinating missed children, including those aged 24-35 months.

papers.title: Associations between different intensities of leisure-time physical activity and subsequent psychotropic medication use among young and early midlife adults: a register-linked follow-up study
papers.abstract: IntroductionPrevious studies have not examined associations between physical activity intensity and subsequent psychotropic medication use. We examined associations between different leisure-time physical activity (LTPA) intensities and subsequent psychotropic medication purchases. MethodsWe used Helsinki Health Study questionnaire data collected in 2017 from 19-39-year-old employees of the City of Helsinki, linked to register data on psychotropic medication purchases from 2014 to 2022 (82.5% consented to the register linkage). The analytical sample included 4,160 participants (80.4% women, representing the target population). Weekly hours of light (LPA), moderate (MPA) and vigorous (VPA) LTPA were examined separately. Cox proportional hazards regression with restricted cubic splines was used to examine nonlinear associations with the first psychotropic medication purchase during follow-up, adjusting for prior medication and sociodemographic and health-related covariates. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported. ResultsDuring the follow-up, 28.1% of participants had at least one psychotropic medication purchase. After adjustment for age and gender, VPA was associated with psychotropic medication purchases (overall p<0.001; nonlinearity p<0.001), whereas MPA and LPA were not. Further adjustments and stratification by prior psychotropic medication purchase status attenuated the VPA association (overall p=0.0041). In this model, for 5 versus 0 hours/week of VPA, the HR was 0.79 (95% CI 0.68-0.91), corresponding to approximately 23 fewer first-purchase events per 1,000 participants over three years. ConclusionsHigher-intensity LTPA appeared more strongly associated with a lower hazard of psychotropic medication purchases, although only the VPA association saw clear support.

papers.title: Beyond the 24-Hour Rhythm: Functional Principal Components of Daily Activity Residuals and Mortality in NHANES
papers.abstract: BackgroundAccelerometer-derived 24-hour activity profiles are usually summarised by cosinor rhythm parameters or by functional principal component analysis (FPCA). Applied to the raw profiles, however, the leading functional components largely re-express what the cosinor already captures: activity level, rhythm strength and timing. Whether the shape of the day carries health information beyond these parameters is unclear. MethodsWe analysed adults with seven valid days of accelerometry from two National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) cohorts: hip activity counts (2003-2006; n = 2,615) and wrist Monitor-Independent Movement Summary units (2011-2014; n = 3,208). Minute-level activity was transformed with the inverse hyperbolic sine, and a single 24-hour cosinor curve was fitted across each participants seven days. Each participants average residual curve, which contains no 24-hour component, was decomposed by FPCA and, to separate stable between-person patterns from day-to-day variation, by multilevel FPCA. In exploratory analyses, we related the three leading components to all-cause mortality and, secondarily, to cardiovascular and cancer mortality. We used Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, income and the cosinor parameters, with the hip cohort for discovery and the wrist cohort for replication. ResultsThe three leading residual components explained 44% (hip) and 51% (wrist) of residual variance and consisted mainly of 12-hour and 8-hour patterns. The second component (FPC2) contrasts an early-starting, flat day with a day of distinct mid-morning and evening peaks. Its shape was nearly identical in the two cohorts (similarity 0.96), and multilevel FPCA recovered it as a stable between-person pattern. In unweighted models, FPC2 was the only component associated with all-cause mortality in the discovery cohort (hazard ratio per SD 1.17, 95% CI 1.06 to 1.29; Benjamini-Hochberg q = 0.008), and the association replicated in the wrist cohort (1.18, 1.03 to 1.35; p = 0.017). With survey weights that also accounted for selection into the analytic sample, the association was concentrated in cardiovascular deaths (hip 1.53, 1.12 to 2.09, p = 0.007; wrist 1.38, 1.10 to 1.72, p = 0.005). This association persisted after further adjustment for lifestyle factors and traditional activity metrics. FPC2 was not associated with cancer mortality. Scores of the leading components did not form distinct clusters (average silhouette width[≤] 0.23), but FPC2 was selected as a continuous predictor of cardiovascular mortality in both cohorts by forward selection on 10-fold cross-validated, survey-weighted AUC. ConclusionsThe within-day structure of activity that a 24-hour cosinor cannot represent varies continuously between people. One replicated aspect of it, the loss of a two-peak daily pattern, was associated with mortality beyond rhythm strength and timing, most clearly cardiovascular mortality. The shape of daily activity therefore carries prognostic information beyond standard rhythm summaries. It can support mortality risk prediction that needs only a few personal details, and may help identify individuals at elevated risk and tailor interventions to their daily activity patterns.

papers.title: Resting Heart Rate for Global Health Surveillance: Descriptive Epidemiology of 566,986 Participants from the WHO STEP Surveys and the South Asia Biobank
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo describe global patterns of resting heart rate (RHR) in population subgroups and over time. MethodsObservational data from WHO STEP surveys (n=363,462 participants from 76 countries, 2002-2020) and the South Asia Biobank (SAB, n=203,524 participants from four South Asian countries, 2018-2023). RHR was measured in triplicate while seated using a blood pressure cuff. Height and weight were measured using anthropometric techniques. Physical activity was self-reported and accelerometry-measured (SAB subsample, n=22,183). We describe RHR distributions by geographical region, temporality, sex, age, BMI, and physical activity. Utility of RHR to explain accelerometer-based physical activity was examined by regression. ResultsCountry-level median RHR ranged 65-80 bpm, higher in women than men. Age-related RHR patterns diverged markedly by sex; men showing a curvilinear association with higher RHR in midlife, and women showing a consistent decline with age across most regions. Compared to normal-weight, obese participants had higher RHR [WHO: (men: +4.4 bpm, women: +0.9 bpm, SAB: (men: +3.1 bpm, women: +1.0 bpm)]. Participants meeting physical activity recommendations had lower RHR [WHO: (men -1.6 bpm, women: -0.9 bpm), SAB: (men: -2.1 bpm, women: -0.5 bpm)] compared to insufficiently active. In SAB (field-work spanning whole-calendar year), seasonal variations were present (0.6-0.9 bpm higher RHR in June-August compared to the Sept-Nov period), most pronounced further from the equator. In 21 WHO countries with repeat survey data, RHR was stable over time in women but declined in men (-0.4 bpm/year). Self-reported activity explained 2-14% (women: 2-3%, men: 10-14%) of the variance in device-measured physical activity, and RHR added 1-3% incrementally. ConclusionsRHR varies globally, exhibits different age-related patterns by sex, and is higher in population subgroups with greater non-communicable disease burden. RHR is easy to measure and may have utility for global health surveillance.

papers.title: El Nino Southern Oscillation shapes cholera in Africa
papers.abstract: Cholera is considered a paradigm for climate-sensitive diseases, yet its relation with El Nino Southern Oscillation (ENSO), the dominant mode of interannual climate variability, remains poorly quantified in Africa where most cholera deaths occur. Using 15 years of surveillance data across 30 African countries and novel statistical and simulation frameworks, we identify five geographically coherent ENSO-cholera teleconnection groups, each characterized by distinct directions, strengths and timing of effects on outbreak occurrence, duration and incidence. For the unfolding major El Nino of 2026-27, we project two- to five-fold greater cholera burden in Eastern and Horn of Africa than under ENSO-neutral conditions. These findings identify immediate priorities for anticipatory action and establish a dynamic framework for attributing burden for outbreak-prone diseases to climate variability.

papers.title: Factors associated with congenital syphilis among women with gestational syphilis in a public health network in Bogota, Colombia, 2017-2024: A case-control study
papers.abstract: BackgroundCongenital syphilis remains a preventable cause of perinatal morbidity and mortality, and its incidence in Colombia remains well above the elimination target. We aimed to identify maternal and prenatal care factors associated with congenital syphilis among women with gestational syphilis attended in a public health network serving socially vulnerable populations in Bogota, Colombia. MethodsWe conducted a retrospective case-control study using surveillance and clinical records from the Subred Integrada de Servicios de Salud Sur E.S.E. for pregnancies ending between 2017 and 2024. Cases were neonates with congenital syphilis according to national surveillance criteria; controls were neonates without congenital syphilis born to mothers with gestational syphilis in the same network. Factors associated with congenital syphilis were identified using multivariable logistic regression with backward elimination. ResultsWe included 743 mother-infant pairs (285 cases and 458 controls). Maternal diagnosis after 28 weeks of gestation (adjusted odds ratio 17.75; 95% confidence interval 11.81-26.69), absence of prenatal care compared with eight or more visits (12.74; 5.03-32.25) and reinfection during pregnancy (3.02; 1.73-5.29) were independently associated with congenital syphilis, whereas a documented history of syphilis was associated with lower odds (0.45; 0.25-0.82). The model showed high discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.860). Migrant status was associated with congenital syphilis in the crude analysis but not after adjustment. ConclusionsCongenital syphilis in this setting was associated mainly with late maternal diagnosis and absent prenatal care, conditions that preclude timely benzathine penicillin treatment. Strengthening early prenatal screening, continuity of care and partner management may reduce vertical transmission in socially vulnerable urban populations.

papers.title: Discrete dynamic survival analysis of epidemic case line lists
papers.abstract: Case line lists, which record dates of onset, recovery, and hospitalisation, are among the most granular data in infectious disease epidemiology and can provide insights into transmission dynamics. Dynamic survival analysis (DSA) fits a deterministic, differential-equation-based model to line lists to estimate parameters such as infectivity and the infectious period. Infectious periods are usually not exponential, and incorporating this into mechanistic models for line-list data often requires partial differential equation (PDE) schemes that can be difficult to implement and must be customised for each model, which may limit their use. Here, we propose Discrete Dynamic Survival Analysis (DDSA), a discrete-time DSA for case line lists based on difference equations. It matches calendar-day data directly without interpolation, and its log-likelihood is differentiable via forward-mode automatic differentiation, enabling off-the-shelf gradient-based samplers without model-specific numerical infrastructure. Non-exponential infectious periods are accommodated through a boxcar model or a discrete analogue of the "device of stages". We apply the DDSA method to three historical outbreaks of influenza A(H1N1), Ebola, and measles. DDSA estimates of transmission parameters were close to published analyses where these were available, an agreement that partly reflects shared modelling choices, and the method handles incomplete line lists with missing onset or recovery dates. Synthetic experiments show that recovery intervals identify the infectious period, while infection times and final size constrain R0 when the population at risk is known. Discrete DSA provides a simple, extensible framework for simulation and inference of infectious disease dynamics.

papers.title: Influenza Vaccination and Disease Severity Among Older Adults Hospitalized with Influenza in France: A Nationwide Cohort Study, 2016-2024
papers.abstract: ObjectiveSeasonal influenza remains a major cause of severe morbidity and mortality among older adults, despite vaccine availability. We assessed whether influenza vaccination was associated with reduced disease severity among adults aged [≥]65 years hospitalized with influenza in France. Methods and AnalysisWe conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using the French National Health Data System (SNDS). Adults aged [≥]65 years hospitalized with confirmed influenza (ICD-10 codes: J09 or J10) between October 2016 and December 2024 were included, excluding 2020-2021. Vaccination status was identified from reimbursed community pharmacy dispensing records. Entropy balancing was used to balance sociodemographic characteristics, chronic conditions pneumococcal vaccination, and COVID-19 vaccination. Weighted regression models estimated adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) for invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), intensive care unit (ICU) admission, in-hospital death, and a composite severe outcome. Multistate survival models assessed transitions specific hazard ratios (HR) between hospitalization, ICU, discharge, and in-hospital death. ResultsAmong 132,443 influenza-associated hospitalizations, 72,852 (55%) occurred among vaccinated patients and 59,591 (45%) among unvaccinated patients. Vaccinated patients were older (mean age, 82.3 vs 79.3 years). IMV occurred in 2128 vaccinated (2.9%) and 2544 unvaccinated (4.3%) hospitalizations (aRR, 0.88; 95%CI: 0.83 to 0.93). In-hospital death occurred in 6300 (8.6%) and 4952 (8.3%), respectively (aRR, 0.90; 95%CI: 0.87 to 0.93). Vaccination was also associated with a lower risk of the composite outcome (aRR, 0.96; 95%CI: 0.94 to 0.98), but not ICU admission (aRR, 0.99; 95%CI: 0.96 to 1.01). Among patients admitted to ICU, vaccination was associated with a lower hazard of death (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.85; 95%CI: 0.78 to 0.92) and a 2-day reduction in the median time to discharge. ConclusionIn this nationwide cohort study, influenza vaccination was associated with lower risks of IMV and in-hospital death among older adults hospitalized with influenza. These findings are consistent with possible attenuation of disease severity and support efforts to improve influenza vaccination among older adults.

papers.title: Associations of drinking water per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances with cause-specific mortality in men with prostate cancer
papers.abstract: BackgroundOver 3.5 million US men are living with prostate cancer (PCa). Certain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are carcinogenic and impair cardiometabolic health. Due to comorbidities and treatment, men with PCa may be uniquely susceptible to PFAS. ObjectivesTo develop and validate a model for drinking water perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS), and perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA), and study associations of each PFAS with all-cause, PCa, and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality in PCa survivors. MethodsWe conducted a cohort study of 51,289 men with PCa diagnosed from 2006 to 2017 and followed through 2024 from the New Jersey (NJ) cancer registry. PFAS monitoring data (n=26,161 results) were obtained from NJ government evaluations and Community Water Systems (CWS) compliance reports and were used to estimate PFAS concentrations using a two-phase XGBoost model with 67 predictors of PFAS contamination across 566 CWS. PFAS predictions between 2006-2024 were linked to participants address histories. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated from Cox models with sociodemographic, clinical and time-varying neighborhood covariates. ResultsThere were 19,749 deaths, including 3,778 PCa deaths, and 4,972 CVD deaths over 466,843 person-years. Higher PFOA exposure was associated with all-cause mortality in certain quintiles (aHRQ2vsQ1: 1.07, 95% CI: 1.07-1.12; aHRQ3vsQ1: 1.06, 95% CI: 1.01-1.11) and with CVD mortality (aHRQ5vsQ1: 1.12, 95% CI: 1.01-1.24). Higher PFNA exposure was suggestively associated with all-cause mortality (aHR[≥]3.8ng/L vs <2ng/L: 1.22, 95% CI: 0.98-1.50) and PCa mortality (aHR[≥]3.8ng/L vs <2ng/L: 1.42, 95% CI: 0.96-2.10). Associations were strengthened when applying five-year lags. For example, higher PFOA (aHRQ5vsQ1: 1.15, 95% CI: 1.06-1.25), PFOS (aHRQ5vsQ1: 1.16, 95% CI: 1.07-1.25) and PFNA (aHR[≥]3.8ng/Lvs <2ng/L: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.06-2.31) were associated with higher all-cause mortality. DiscussionExposure to CWS-level PFAS was associated with higher mortality in PCa survivors. Replication is needed to confirm findings.

papers.title: Sex-Specific Incidence of Hemorrhagic Stroke in Japan: An Integrated Population-Based Study
papers.abstract: BackgroundIntracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) have contrasting epidemiological characteristics, including sex-specific incidence. However, their overall contribution to sex differences in hemorrhagic stroke remains unclear because they are generally evaluated separately. We examined the sex-specific epidemiology of hemorrhagic stroke by integrating ICH and SAH. MethodsWe analyzed first-ever ICH and SAH events recorded from 2011 through 2015 in the Shiga Stroke and Heart Attack Registry, a population-based registry covering approximately 1.4 million residents in Japan. Age-specific and age-adjusted incidence rates were calculated by sex and stroke subtype using direct standardization to the 2015 Japanese Census population. ResultsAmong 4,517 patients with hemorrhagic stroke, 3,461 (76.6%) had ICH and 1,056 (23.4%) had SAH. The age-adjusted incidence of ICH was higher in men than in women (61.2 vs 49.8 per 100,000 person-years), whereas SAH incidence was more than twice as high in women as in men (22.4 vs 10.4 per 100,000 person-years). Despite these opposing patterns, the age-adjusted incidence of hemorrhagic stroke was nearly identical between men and women (71.6 vs 72.2 per 100,000 person-years). ICH accounted for a greater share of the overall incidence among men, whereas SAH accounted for a greater share among women. ConclusionsDespite marked subtype-specific sex differences, the overall incidence of hemorrhagic stroke was similar between women and men. These findings demonstrate that substantial sex differences in individual subtypes may be offset when ICH and SAH are considered together, highlighting the value of an integrated population-level perspective in evaluating sex disparities in hemorrhagic stroke.

papers.title: Unraveling the genetic architecture of the human mammillary bodies
papers.abstract: The mammillary bodies are a central component of the hippocampal-diencephalic-cingulate network that is critically involved in emotion processing and memory function, yet their genetic architecture remains unknown. We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of mammillary body volume in 38,064 participants from the UK Biobank and replicated our findings in the Rhineland Study cohort (N = 4,860). Mammillary body and hypothalamic subregional volumes were derived from structural brain MRIs using FastSurfer-HypVINN, an established and validated deep learning-based segmentation tool. Univariate GWAS identified 34 genomic loci associated with mammillary body volume, including 26 novel loci, with 20 loci showing replication in the Rhineland Study. Meta-analysis across both cohorts (N = 42,924) identified 44 associated loci, of which 35 were novel. Multivariate GWAS of hypothalamic subregions identified 55 loci, including 40 novel associations. Integrative cross-omics analyses identified MEI1 and CAPZA1 as key molecular candidates, with genetically regulated MEI1 expression and circulating CAPZA1 protein levels partially mediating genetic effects on mammillary body volume. Genetic correlation and Mendelian randomization analyses further revealed a bidirectional relationship between mammillary body volume and major depressive disorder. Together, our findings elucidate the genetic architecture of mammillary body volume and its relation to mental disorders.

papers.title: Lipidome-wide analysis of concurrent and longitudinal blood pressure patterns in school-aged children
papers.abstract: BackgroundElevated blood pressure (BP) in childhood is associated with cardiovascular risk, but its molecular lipid correlates remain poorly characterized. We investigated the association of plasma lipid species and patterns with concurrent and longitudinal BP phenotypes in school-aged children. MethodsIn the Belgian ENVIRONAGE prospective birth-cohort, 195 children aged 9 to 12 years were examined between July 2021 and September 2024. A total of 1,232 plasma lipid species were quantified using liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization-tandem mass spectrometry. Associations with systolic and diastolic BP percentiles were examined using multivariable linear regression with permutation-based family-wise error rate (FWER) correction. Lipid-set enrichment analysis, with P values from sample permutation to account for correlation among lipid species, evaluated coordinated associations. Significant findings were examined across longitudinal BP patterns in 177 children with BP measured at ages 4-6 and 9-12. FindingsEach 1-SD increase in triglyceride (TG) 58:9 fatty acyl (FA) 22:4 was associated with 7.36 higher systolic BP percentile points (95% CI=3.91-10.80; PFWER=0.03). TG 58:9 FA 22:4 was associated with incident (OR=2.78; 95% CI=1.33-5.79) and persistent (OR=2.14; 95% CI=1.22-3.77), but not resolved elevated BP vs stable-normal BP. Among lipid sets, species with a total carbon number of 38, mainly PC and PE, were inversely enriched with diastolic BP percentile. InterpretationChildhood BP was associated with higher levels of a highly polyunsaturated long-chain TG, closely related to current BP elevation and not elevated among children whose BP had normalized. FundingSpecial Research Fund, Flemish Scientific Research Fund, Methusalem and Kom op Tegen Kanker. Research in contextO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSWe searched PubMed for studies published from inception to 13 October 2026, without language restrictions, for human studies, using the following combinations of terms: ("child*" OR "adolescen*") AND ("blood pressure" OR "hypertension") AND ("lipidomic*" OR "lipidome"). Previous pediatric studies have implicated glycerophospholipids, sphingolipids and triglycerides, but most were conducted in specific clinical, dietary, environmental, or ethnic settings. We found little population-based evidence from comprehensive lipidome-wide analyses and no studies examining whether lipidomic signatures differ according to longitudinal blood pressure patterns spanning early and later childhood. Added value of this studyIn a population-based birth cohort, we measured 1,232 lipid species in plasma from 195 children aged 9-12 years and related them to blood pressure at that age and at ages 4-6 years. One long-chain, highly unsaturated triglyceride was associated with higher systolic blood pressure. The triglyceride association was present in children whose blood pressure became or remained elevated, but not in those whose elevated blood pressure had normalized. Accounting for the correlation among lipids, only one lipid group, phospholipids with 38 carbon atoms, was inversely enriched with diastolic blood pressure. Implications of all the available evidenceTogether with adult studies linking triglyceride species to hypertension, our findings suggest that a triglyceride species is also associated with blood pressure in children. The lead triglyceride species was more closely related to current elevation, and was not detectable in children with normal current blood pressure but earlier elevation. Smaller signatures of earlier blood pressure cannot be excluded, studies with repeated lipidomics and blood pressure assessment from early childhood are needed to determine whether earlier blood pressure leaves a more subtle trace in the lipidome.

papers.title: Effect of starting metformin on severe and long COVID-19 among people living with type 2 diabetes in England: a new user cohort study in OpenSAFELY-TPP
papers.abstract: IntroductionObservational studies report lower COVID-19 mortality among metformin users, but most used prevalent-user designs comparing long-term survivors with heterogeneous controls. Randomised trials suggest little or no mortality effect. No large observational study has used a new-user design to estimate the effect of starting versus not starting metformin on severe and Long COVID outcomes in adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D). We aimed to estimate this effect on COVID-19-related hospitalisation or death, COVID-19 diagnoses, and Long COVID among adults with T2D in England. Research design and methodsUsing OpenSAFELY-TPP linked NHS electronic health records, we conducted a population-based cohort study with a landmark new-user design. Adults aged 18-85 years newly diagnosed with T2D (August 2018-August 2019) were classified as starting metformin monotherapy within 6 months or not starting any antidiabetic drug, based on prescription data. Follow-up began 6 months after diagnosis and before the UK pandemic (avoiding immortal time) for up to 2 years. We estimated intention-to-treat and per-protocol effects using weighted Cox and pooled logistic regression, with negative (bone fracture) and positive (diabetes-related death) control outcomes. ResultsOf 52,341 eligible people, 19,599 (37.4%) started metformin. For COVID-19-related hospitalisation or death, the maximally adjusted hazard ratio (HR) of metformin versus no antidiabetic was 1.17 (95% CI 1.02-1.35; 2-year risk difference 0.36%, 95% CI 0.09-0.62; intention-to-treat). The per-protocol HR for COVID-19-related hospitalisation or death was 1.11 (95% CI 0.96-1.29). The Long COVID estimate was imprecise (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.83-2.33; intention-to-treat). For bone fracture (negative control) the estimate was null (HR 1.00), but for diabetes-related deaths (positive control) it was elevated (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.09-1.81), indicating unmeasured confounding. ConclusionsThe risks of severe and long COVID were slightly higher among people who started metformin, compared with those who did not start. These results plausibly reflect unmeasured confounding. These findings align more closely with randomised evidence than earlier prevalent-user studies and argue against a clinically meaningful benefit of starting metformin for COVID-19 prevention in newly diagnosed T2D. What is already known on this topicObservational studies and their meta-analyses have consistently reported 30-40% lower COVID-19 mortality among metformin users, yet most used prevalent-user designs that compare long-term survivors with mixed control groups and can overstate benefit. Randomised trials suggest little or no effect on mortality. What this study addsUsing a new-user design in more than 52,000 adults with newly diagnosed T2D, risks of severe and long COVID were slightly higher among people who started metformin, compared with those who did not start. These results plausibly reflect unmeasured confounding rather than harm. How this study might affect research, practice or policyThese findings align with randomised evidence and argue against a clinically meaningful benefit of starting metformin for preventing severe or Long COVID in people with T2D. They also illustrate how new-user designs can reconcile discrepant observational and trial results and should be prioritised in future drug-repurposing studies. Lay summaryMetformin is a medication commonly used to treat type 2 diabetes. During the COVID-19 pandemic, some studies suggested it might also protect against severe COVID-19, but many such studies had design limitations that could have made metformin look more beneficial than it truly is. In this study, we used NHS health records from over 52,000 adults in England who were newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes to examine whether starting metformin shortly after diagnosis reduced the risk of being hospitalised or dying from COVID-19, being diagnosed with COVID-19. We found no evidence that starting metformin protected against any of these outcomes, although the effect on long COVID was imprecisely estimated. Our findings are consistent with results from clinical trials and suggest that metformin should not be expected to prevent severe COVID-19 in people with type 2 diabetes.
